plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs covered in rose-like blooms, with tightly layered petals that glow against dark leaves. Camellias flower while most of the garden is still dormant, so they stand out in the winter landscape.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter into early spring, typically January through April depending on cultivar and weather
plants.location: Temperate gardens of the Northern Hemisphere, including Japan, the southern United States and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Both belong to the same genus.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A broad, flat-topped tree with feathery foliage. In flower, its crown is covered in blazing scarlet-orange blossoms, making a spectacular tropical canopy.
plants.location: Hawaiʻi, USA, and other tropical regions
plants.funFact: Botanist Dr. Hillebrand introduced the royal poinciana to Hawaiʻi in 1855. It is now a favorite shade tree there.
